headline: Completed historic survey suggests seven Biddeford properties could be considered for National Register listing.
summary: The Klein Foundation survey recommends more work to find historic properties outside the local district. A list of the properties will be made, and the group will decide how to rank them. The group also raised a $275 application fee and a possible fee based on construction costs.
discussion: Survey follow-up: The survey suggested more work is needed outside the local historic district. Seven properties were named as possible National Register candidates, including the Obit Amory House and the former Bitterbird High School, now the Martin Center.
Application fee: The $275 application fee was called too high for small projects and too low for large ones. A fee based on a percentage of construction costs was suggested.

Mayor's committee report: The chair drafted the annual report for the mayor's office and asked members for changes. Two times this year the commission lacked a quorum, and a meeting had to be delayed.
Meeting time and recruiting: Members discussed a meeting time later than 4 p.m. and better marketing to attract new members.
Historic signs: A generic sign for the district's perimeter was discussed, and public works would provide materials only. One member and staff will map where the signs should go.
